scope: Ordinary Core current-instance recovery on macOS; original web address, original backend port and same Core PID across exec.

architecture.progress: Scoped read-only SSE; bounded reconnection and synchronization after reconnect, no periodic page status queries

browser.backend: Real ordinary Core with owned PostgreSQL and Redis, through production Nuxt proxy
checks: Restore from page without changing the website origin
Progress resumes across normal-to-maintenance and maintenance-to-normal exec
Authenticated refresh can reopen the completed job
No recovery credentials in URL, localStorage or sessionStorage
No periodic catalog requests while idle

source_validation.capability_check: passed earlier in this implementation; no capability contract changed

resolved_failures: Public browser Origin did not match rewritten upstream Host; validate public same-origin first, then translate both to the backend origin
After upstream exec interrupted an already-started SSE stream, h3 left the downstream response open; explicitly close it so the browser reconnects
Temporary file preparation failure now removes this attempt's prepared neighbors before any target overwrite

cleanup.retained_failed_fixtures: 30 old process records checked; no owned fixture service alive. Four owned temporary data directories removed after preserving diagnostics.

supported_auto_integration.redis: Explicit registered logical databases must have no other clients; protection snapshot captures them

limitations: Production auto-integrated overwrite remains blocked; this is not acceptance for remote production upgrade
Linux, Docker/systemd real deployment and live production plugins have not been accepted
Online packages lacking a same-point Redis image are dev data rehearsal only; registered exclusive logical databases are reset, not historical Redis queue replay
Retained native UI fixture validates transport and status; native A/B test separately asserts database, media and config differences
Current runtime can retain the new Core maintenance adapter for older dev snapshots that do not implement the current recovery protocol; that is not byte-for-byte old Core program replay
If the entire Core process is manually stopped, the original launch must first start it; maintenance does not claim to serve HTTP without a process
